narrative.overview:
Every manual task in a business is a printed docket. The site is a pass in a busy kitchen or a print shop: a cool paper ground, white thermal dockets clipped to a brushed-stainless rail, printed in black. A single printer red marks the moment work changes hands from a person to a system: the strike through a manual task, the AUTOMATED stamp, the line that says it now runs by itself, and the one action that starts the job. The world is literal and material. Paper has grain, torn serrated edges, and a soft shadow. Steel has a brushed raster and a highlight. Nothing is glass, and no surface wears a decorative color gradient.

Density is a working counter's, not a gallery's. Big condensed display type in uppercase does the shouting. Hanken Grotesk carries plain-English explanation at a readable measure. Martian Mono appears only where a printer would have printed: on dockets, receipts, slips, filed jobs, and the done tag. The page is light only; there is no dark theme.

One piece of motion defines the world. The hero docket prints in steps, its manual lines are struck through in red one after another, it is stamped AUTOMATED, and it slides to the done spike. It runs once when it comes into view, can be replayed, and is shown already finished under reduced motion or without JavaScript. Every other element simply sits on the page.
keyCharacteristics: Cool paper ground, white textured dockets with serrated edges, brushed-steel rail and spikes.
Print black plus one red; red means "changed or automated" and "act here", nothing else.
Printer discipline on dockets: two sizes, rank by weight, caps, red ink, and reversed black bars.
Square corners everywhere paper and ink meet; small radii only on steel hardware.
Depth comes from paper lifting off paper (drop-shadow on the torn silhouette), not from cards.
One signature sequence (print, strike, stamp, file) and no other entrance animation.

rules.name: The Red Means Automated Rule
rules.body: Red is reserved for strikes, the AUTOMATED stamp, the "Runs by itself" after-line, the Result label in filed jobs, the tear-off stub, error states, text selection, and the RON wordmark block. Flags, checkmarks, step numbers, link underlines, and hovers are ink or reversed, never red. If a new element wants red, ask whether it shows work that now runs by itself or is the one action to take; if not, it is ink.

rules.name: The Reversed Bar Rule
rules.body: Emphasis is reversed printing (white on Print Black), not a new color. Docket bars, flags, tags, filed-job sides, and hover fills all reverse.

rules.name: The Printer's Voice Rule
rules.body: Monospace appears only on docket surfaces (dockets, receipt, filed jobs, slips, done tag), prose table headers and inline code, and timeline dates. Labels anywhere else are Hanken Grotesk, uppercase, tracked. Explanatory sentences that sit on a docket (stage descriptions, agenda items) switch back to Hanken Grotesk.

rules.name: The Two Sizes Rule
rules.body: On a docket, rank by weight, caps, reversal, and red ink, not by adding sizes. A docket carries its mono size and at most one display title.

rules.name: The Torn Silhouette Rule
rules.body: A paper surface's edge is a mask, its shadow is a drop-shadow filter. Never box-shadow a torn edge.

dos: Do put new content on paper objects that hang from or file off the rail: dockets, slips, receipts, filed jobs.
Do cut paper edges with a conic-gradient mask on `::before` and shadow them with the paper-lift drop-shadow filter on the element.
Do reverse to Print Black for emphasis, flags, bars, and hover fills.
Do keep red to the eight reserved uses in The Red Means Automated Rule; use Deep Printer Red when red is small text on white.
Do set dockets in Martian Mono with tabular numerals at the 42-column module, and switch explanatory sentences on them back to Hanken Grotesk.
Do keep corners square on paper, ink, and controls; reserve small radii for steel hardware.
Do ship any new motion as a finished state first, with a reduced-motion path that shows the end.
donts: Don't use red for flags, checkmarks, step numbers, link underlines, or hover states (the stub deepening to Deep Printer Red is the one red hover, because the stub is already red).
Don't set labels in monospace off docket surfaces; use Hanken Grotesk uppercase tracked.
Don't add entrance animations beyond the docket sequence; all other motion is state feedback (hovers, the stub tear, the FAQ plus, rail scrolling).
Don't box-shadow a torn edge or add rectangular card shadows to paper.
Don't introduce a second accent color, decorative color gradients, glass, or a dark theme. (Gradients used as drawing tools, such as perforations, masks, and the rail's shade, are native.)
Don't add rounded corners to dockets, buttons, or inputs.
